text: Build agent workflows without writing code
quote: Build AI agents that use your tools and data to get real work done—no code required.

text: Tell an agent in plain language to update its own instructions or save behavior as a skill
quote: tell it: "Update your instructions so you always do it this way" or "Turn this into a skill."

text: Schedule agents to run on a recurring or one-time basis
quote: Schedule your agent to run automatically on a recurring schedule or as a one-time trigger.

text: Trigger agents automatically from events in connected external apps
quote: app triggers to fire when something happens in an external service

text: Give an agent a webhook URL so any HTTP POST (Stripe, GitHub, cron job, script) can start it
quote: A webhook trigger gives an agent its own URL. Anything that can send an HTTP POST — Stripe, GitHub, a cron job, an internal script — runs the agent by calling it.

text: Outbound webhooks let Gumloop notify your own systems when events occur
quote: Outbound webhooks let Gumloop notify **your** systems when something happens in your organization.

text: Skills are reusable instruction packs that teach agents how to do specific tasks and improve over time
quote: A **skill** is a reusable set of instructions (and optionally templates and scripts) that teaches an agent how to do a specific task.

text: Admins can centrally manage organization-wide skills and keep them synced with a GitHub repo
quote: Centrally manage skills for your whole organization, and keep them in sync with a GitHub repository.

text: Require human approval before an agent performs sensitive actions like sending email or deleting records
quote: Instead of blindly trusting every tool call, you can require approval for sensitive operations like sending emails, creating repositories, or deleting records.

text: Run Python code and shell commands in an isolated cloud sandbox as part of an agent
quote: The Code Sandbox gives your agent the ability to execute Python code and shell commands in a secure, isolated cloud environment.

text: Connect an agent to any MCP-compatible server to extend it with specialized tools
quote: Gumloop supports connecting to any [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://www.gumloop.com/blog/what-is-mcp-model-context-protocol-a-simple-guide) server. This lets you extend your agents with specialized tools, internal services, or any MCP

text: Proxy existing external MCP servers into Gumloop through a managed proxy
quote: Proxied MCPs let you connect existing, external MCP servers to Gumloop through a managed proxy.

text: Build and host custom MCP servers on Gumloop's own infrastructure
quote: Hosted MCPs let your organization build and deploy custom MCP servers on Gumloop's infrastructure. You write the code in a GitHub repository, and Gumloop handles building, deploying, monitoring, and routing requests to your server.

text: API supports two authentication methods that grant identical permissions on every endpoint
quote: The Gumloop API supports two authentication methods. Both grant the same permissions and work on every endpoint — pick whichever matches how your app gets the credential.

text: Team (workspace) API keys are scoped to a single team
quote: Team (workspace) API keys are scoped to a single team.

text: OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint routes to any supported model (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter)
quote: client.chat.completions.create(...) is an OpenAI-compatible chat surface that routes to every model Gumloop supports (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter routes).

text: Official Python and JavaScript SDKs let you build against Gumloop from your own code
quote: Build on Gumloop from your own code with the Python and JavaScript SDKs

text: Bring your own API keys for connected services
quote: Bring Your Own API Keys

text: Some integrations work out of the box via a Gumloop-managed API key without user setup
quote: add one to an agent and it works on the first run, either because the data is public or because Gumloop supplies a managed API key behind the scenes

text: API lets you create/update agents, start chat sessions, and run chat completions
quote: you can create and update agents, start sessions to chat with them, and use chat completions

text: Supports OAuth 2.0 for building apps that other Gumloop users sign in to
quote: Gumloop supports OAuth 2.0, which is recommended if you're building an application that other Gumloop users sign in to.

text: Generate a connector-scoped token from the Connectors page and use it as a bearer token
quote: Generate one from the Connectors page, then pass it as a bearer token.

text: Create new agents programmatically via the API, with permission checks per team
quote: Create a new agent. The authenticated caller must have permission to create agents on the target team.

text: Connect prebuilt integrations like Gmail, Salesforce, and Slack to an agent
quote: Open the Connectors section and add the integrations the agent needs (Gmail, Salesforce, Slack, and so on).

text: Auto-deploy agent code on every push to the GitHub main branch via the Gumloop GitHub App
quote: Install the Gumloop GitHub App on your GitHub organization. This enables automatic deployments: every push to your main branch triggers a new build and deploy.

text: Connect agents to Slack channels so teams can interact with them
quote: Connect your Gumloop agents to Slack channels so your entire team can interact with AI-powered assistants in the tools they use every day.

text: Connect agents to Microsoft Teams so anyone can @mention them
quote: Connect your Gumloop agents to Microsoft Teams so anyone in a channel can interact with them using a simple @mention.

text: Give an agent a goal and tools; it autonomously decides which tools to call, in what order, and when to ask for input
quote: You give an agent a goal and a set of tools, and it figures out how to get there: which tools to call, in what order, and when to ask you for input.

text: Self-contained installer ships its own Python and needs no sudo
quote: The installer is fully self-contained under ~/.gumloop — it ships its own Python, never touches your system Python, and needs no sudo.

text: Ask a built-in assistant which candidate model should handle a task before running it
quote: Ask Gumloop Chew which of your candidate models should handle a task. Decision only — nothing runs.

text: Unregistered Slack users can message org agents, which run under a shared service account
quote: people in a Slack workspace you have registered can message those agents with **no Gumloop account at all**, and their requests run on a shared **organization service account** instead of a personal one

text: Files an agent generates (reports, spreadsheets, code, dashboards) are saved as viewable, downloadable, version-tracked artifacts
quote: Reports, spreadsheets, images, code files, HTML dashboards: anything your agent creates can be viewed, downloaded, shared, and version-tracked directly from the chat.

text: Stream agent output in real time via a dedicated streaming API endpoint
quote: To stream agent output as it's produced, send the same request body (with `stream: true`) to the streaming host instead

text: A performance view shows an agent's cost, output quality, and activity history
quote: **Performance** in the agent sidebar answers three questions about one agent: what is it costing, is it doing good work, and what has it actually been doing.

text: Give an agent a dedicated email address so people can interact with it by sending email
quote: Give your agent a dedicated email address so anyone can interact with it by sending an email.

text: Agents have exactly two roles: Owners manage the agent, Users run it
quote: Agents have exactly **two roles**: **Owners** manage the agent, **Users** run it.
